title: Exact native Weil open extension and its clopen direct-image comparison
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For each locally finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal W_T$ be the abelian category of all pro-etale Weil sheaves from [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]: modules over the sheaf $B_{\bar T}$ of locally finite continuous $\Omega$-valued functions on $\bar T=T\times_{k_0}k$, with an isomorphism $F_T^*M\cong M$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of locally finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Its native Frobenius-equivariant extension by zero $j_!:\mathcal W_U\to\mathcal W_X$ is additive and exact. There is a natural transformation $\alpha_j:j_!\to j_*$, with $j_*$ the native ordinary direct image, whose underlying map after forgetting Frobenius is the canonical comparison $\bar j_!\to\bar j_*$. If $j$ is also universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], then $\alpha_j$ is a natural isomorphism. These assertions concern all sheaves in $\mathcal W_U$, with no constructibility assumption.

proof.text: Put $A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(B_{\bar T})$ and $P_T=F_T^*$. Use the module description in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], these are abelian categories with all small limits and colimits in the common module universe. Reindexing the site along the scheme automorphisms $F_T$ and $F_T^{-1}$ gives inverse additive equivalences: on functions the coefficient identifications are precomposition by mutually inverse homeomorphisms, which preserve local finite-dimensional span. Thus [lem-sf-fixed-pair-created-abelian-structure] applies to $P_T$. Forgetting Frobenius is additive, creates kernels and cokernels, reflects exactness, and reflects isomorphisms. In particular the underlying inverse of an invertible commuting morphism commutes with Frobenius.

The base change $\bar j$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. The localized-site and coefficient identifications in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] identify its ordinary module extension with $L=P_{(-)}^\#$. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to $(\bar X_{\mathrm{proet}},B_{\bar X})$ at $\bar U$: $L$ is exact. It is additive since on each summand its map sends $u+v$ to $u(s)+v(s)$, and the induced sheaf map is determined by this presheaf map. The native lift has underlying functor $L$ and structure $L(\phi)c_{!,M}$ by the framework. A short exact sequence in $\mathcal W_U$ forgets to a short exact sequence; applying $L$ keeps it short exact; reflection of exactness from Step 1 proves exactness in $\mathcal W_X$. The same underlying-map calculation, and faithful additive forgetting, prove additivity. No quasi-compactness or constructibility was used.

proof.text: Write $R=\bar j_*$, so $(RM)(V)=M(V_U)$, $V_U=V\times_{\bar X}\bar U$, by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and the coefficient action in the framework. Define $P_M\to RM$ as follows. For each factorization $a:V\to\bar U$, the corresponding summand $M(V,a)$ maps by the identification $V_U\cong V$ to $M(V_U)$; if no factorization exists the source is zero. Restricting along $V'\to V$ gives precisely the same section on $V'_U$, so this is a natural presheaf module map. Its action is $B(V)$-linear by restriction of the coefficient functions. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] it extends uniquely to $\alpha_M:LM\to RM$. For $u:M\to N$, both composites with this presheaf map send $s$ to $u(s)$; uniqueness gives $R(u)\alpha_M=\alpha_N L(u)$. This is the canonical comparison, identity after restriction to the open, equivalently the map of the adjoint triple described in the source.

proof.text:
Let $c_!:P_XL\cong LP_U$ and $c_*:P_XR\cong RP_U$ be the framework's Frobenius reindexings. The rule in Step 3 is unchanged by this reindexing: a factorization $V\to\bar U$ corresponds to its Frobenius translate, $V_U$ corresponds to the translated intersection, and its section maps to that same translated section. Thus on every presheaf summand the two maps agree, and the sheafification universal property gives $c_{*,M}P_X(\alpha_M)=\alpha_{P_UM}c_{!,M}$. For a fixed pair $(M,\phi)$, naturality from Step 3 now gives
$$\alpha_M L(\phi)c_{!,M}=R(\phi)\alpha_{P_UM}c_{!,M}=R(\phi)c_{*,M}P_X(\alpha_M).$$
This is exactly the fixed-pair morphism condition. Underlying naturality then gives the natural transformation $\alpha_j:j_!\to j_*$, forgetting to $\alpha$.

Suppose $j$ is universally closed. Its geometric base change is a closed map by the definition in [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $\bar j(\bar U)$ is closed; it is already open by Step 2. Let $Z$ be its open complement. Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] to the two clopen pieces with $R=B_{\bar X}$. Its exact equivalence identifies module restriction to $\bar U$ with first projection and reconstructs a tuple $(M,N)$ by the stated product of sections on the two intersections. In particular $\bar j_*M$ is the tuple $(M,0)$: the formula for its sections is $M(V_U)$ and a sheaf of modules has zero sections on the empty object. The same tuple represents $\bar j_!M$. Indeed for every $(H_U,H_Z)$ its morphisms to that tuple are computed componentwise, giving
$$\operatorname{Hom}((M,0),(H_U,H_Z))=\operatorname{Hom}(M,H_U).$$
This is the left-adjoint universal property of $L$ from Step 2. The identification is normalized by the identity on $M$, so Step 3's comparison is $(1_M,1_0)$: on objects over $\bar U$ its section rule is the identity, and on objects over $Z$ it is the unique zero-module map. The gluing equivalence therefore makes $\alpha_M$ invertible.

proof.text: Step 4 made every $\alpha_M$ a morphism of fixed pairs. Step 5 makes its underlying map invertible, and Step 1 supplies its inverse in the fixed-pair category. The inverses are natural: multiplying $j_*(u)\alpha_M=\alpha_Nj_!(u)$ by the two inverses gives $j_!(u)\alpha_M^{-1}=\alpha_N^{-1}j_*(u)$. Thus $\alpha_j$ is a natural isomorphism for universally closed $j$. All arguments apply to arbitrary module sheaves; in particular the zero sheaf, the empty open, the identity open and an arbitrary clopen union are included.
